fixes.explanation: Home is it. Luke says a woman named Martha welcomed Jesus into her home (Luke 10:38). She's the one who does the welcoming.
Close, but no tent here. Luke says a woman named Martha welcomed Jesus into her home (Luke 10:38). The word is home, not tent.
Nope, no vineyard in this one. Luke says Martha welcomed Jesus into her home (Luke 10:38). The welcome is into a home, not out in a vineyard.
That's Mary. Luke says she "…sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message." (Luke 10:39) She sits down close to Jesus and listens to Him.

Good guess, since a guest in a house might get that. But Luke doesn't say Mary brings Him anything. She "…sat at the Lord’s feet listening to His message." (Luke 10:39) Listening is what the text shows her doing.

Not quite, friend. The size of the house never comes up. Martha asks, "Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone?" (Luke 10:40) Her complaint is about being left to serve by herself, and I think that's where the sting is.

Fair guess, friend, but surprise guests never come up in the text. Martha asks, "Lord, do You not care that my sister has left me to serve alone?" (Luke 10:40) Her question is about Mary. I bet it stung to be the one left serving.
True. Martha says, "Tell her to help me!" (Luke 10:40) She says it to Jesus, asking Him to be the one to tell Mary.
Three is a nice round number, but Jesus doesn't say it. He says, "But only one thing is necessary." (Luke 10:42) One, not three.

Not true. Martha asks for that (Luke 10:40), but the text doesn't show Jesus sending Mary anywhere. He says Mary "…has chosen the good portion, and it will not be taken away from her." (Luke 10:42) His answer is about the good portion Mary has chosen.
